title: Tomato Risotto
description: An oven-baked tomato and sausage risotto with fennel, basil and optional Parmesan at the table.
imageAlt: Reference photograph of a neatly plated tomato risotto on a white plate, topped with sun-dried tomatoes.
imageCaption: Reference photograph · sun-dried tomato variation · displayed crop
personalNote: Better a little less salty than too salty: we can always add salt, but we can’t remove it. Add Parmesan at the table so we can keep a couple of dairy-free portions for lunch.
equipment: Large oven-safe pot with an oven-safe lid
advancePrep: Air-fry the sausages until fully cooked according to their packet, then cut into thin slices. Pick the basil leaves off their stalks.
importantNotes: Four portions is a provisional serving estimate; the serving count has not yet been confirmed by Pavie. The ingredient quantities are exactly the supplied batch. Prep and cooking times are estimates and exclude air-frying the sausages. Do not wash the risotto rice: its starch makes the risotto creamy. Use a pot and lid that are both oven-safe. Keep Parmesan separate from the lunch portions; choose dairy-free sausages and stock cubes if those portions need to be dairy-free. Protein swap for this batch: 300 g sausage, 500 g chicken, or 500 g of 5% lean pork mince. See “Make it work for you” for the cooking changes.

ingredients.name: Vine-ripened tomatoes
ingredients.note: About 2 packs; slice. Or use 2 packs of salad tomatoes and the sugar below.

ingredients.name: Sausages
ingredients.note: Air-fry until fully cooked, then slice thinly. Choose dairy-free ones for the dairy-free lunch portions.

ingredients.name: Chicken stock cubes
ingredients.note: Check the ingredients if keeping lunch portions dairy-free.

ingredients.name: Black pepper
ingredients.note: Coarsely crushed, or use pepper powder.

ingredients.name: Basil leaves
ingredients.note: Pick the leaves off the stalks.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.note: Use only if substituting salad tomatoes for vine-ripened tomatoes.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.note: Only if needed after tasting; remember Parmesan adds saltiness too.

ingredients.name: Parmesan
ingredients.note: Add to individual servings if wanted. Leave out of the dairy-free lunch portions.

steps.title: Prepare and preheat
steps.description: Peel and chop the garlic and brown onion. Slice the tomatoes. Air-fry the sausages until fully cooked, following their packet instructions, then cut them into thin slices. Preheat the oven to 180°C and boil the measured water.

steps.title: Soften the onion and garlic
steps.description: Put the sliced sausage into an oven-safe pot over medium heat. Add the garlic and onion and fry for 5 minutes, until the onion softens.

steps.title: Cook the tomatoes down
steps.description: Add the sliced tomatoes and chicken stock cubes. If you are using salad tomatoes, add the measured sugar too. Cook for 15 minutes, stirring as needed, until the tomatoes become mushy.

steps.title: Add the rice and fennel
steps.description: Add the unwashed risotto rice and mix it through the tomato sauce. Add the fennel seeds and stir.
steps.tip: Fennel seeds look like cumin but are a little bigger and greener. Fennel and tomato are a classic combination: fennel lifts the tomatoes’ sweetness.

steps.title: Add the water and taste
steps.description: Pour in the boiled water and mix. Taste the liquid: it should be pleasantly salted. Do not worry if it is slightly less salty than you would like, because Parmesan added at the table will bring more saltiness. Add salt only if needed. Bring the pot to the boil.
steps.tip: Better a little under-salted than too salty: you can add salt later, but you can’t remove it.
steps.warning: If you swapped in raw chicken or mince, do not taste the liquid until that meat is fully cooked. You can check and adjust the seasoning after baking.

steps.title: Bake the covered risotto
steps.description: Once the liquid starts boiling, cover with the oven-safe lid and transfer the pot to the preheated oven. Bake for 30 minutes.
steps.doneness: Cooked risotto rice. If using chicken or mince, check that the meat is fully cooked before serving.
steps.tip: For a chicken or mince swap, the centre of the meat should reach 75°C for 30 seconds. If it has not, continue cooking and check again before serving.
steps.warning: Use oven gloves. The pot, lid and handles will be hot, including after they return to the hob.

steps.title: Finish with pepper and basil
steps.description: Take the pot out of the oven carefully. Add the black pepper and the basil leaves you picked off their stalks, and mix them through the risotto.
steps.doneness: Cooked risotto rice in a creamy tomato sauce.
steps.warning: Keep oven gloves nearby: the pot handles are still hot.

steps.title: Serve with Parmesan separately
steps.description: Serve the risotto and add Parmesan to individual plates if wanted. Keep a couple of portions without Parmesan for dairy-free lunches.
steps.tip: Keep the cheese at the table instead of mixing it into the whole pot.

substitutions.title: Swap the protein
substitutions.text: For this original batch, interchange 300 g sausage with 500 g chicken or 500 g of 5% lean pork mince. The numbered ingredient quantities scale with the portion control, but these swap quantities describe the original batch. Air-fry sausage until fully cooked according to its packet, then slice it. For chicken, cut into small pieces and cook it in the pot with the aromatics; it must be fully cooked by the end of baking. For pork mince, break it up in the pot and cook it through before continuing. If using raw chicken or mince, wait until the meat is fully cooked before tasting the cooking liquid.

substitutions.title: Salad tomatoes instead of vine-ripened
substitutions.text: For the original batch, use 2 packs of salad tomatoes and add ½ teaspoon of sugar when cooking the tomatoes down.

substitutions.title: Black pepper
substitutions.text: Coarsely crushed pepper or pepper powder both work.

substitutions.title: Dairy-free lunch portions
substitutions.text: Leave Parmesan off the lunch portions, and choose sausages and stock cubes without dairy ingredients.

troubleshooting.title: Why leave the rice unwashed?
troubleshooting.text: Keeping its starch helps make the risotto creamy.

troubleshooting.title: A little less salty than expected?
troubleshooting.text: That is fine. Parmesan adds saltiness at the table, and you can add a little salt to a dairy-free portion if needed.

storage: Divide the lunch portions into small containers to cool quickly, ideally within 1 hour. Refrigerate and eat within 24 hours. Keep Parmesan separate.
reheating: Reheat once until steaming hot throughout. Stir or turn it during microwave reheating to avoid cold pockets.
foodSafety: Air-fry the sausages until fully cooked before slicing. Use an oven-safe pot and lid, and remember the handles stay hot after baking.
servingSuggestion: Parmesan at the table, with a couple of portions kept without cheese for lunch.
